error.signature: AI tells a disaster survivor they must apply for or accept an SBA disaster loan before FEMA will give them Individual Assistance, or that an SBA referral can simply be ignored with no consequence

verdict.summary: For disasters declared on or after March 22, 2024, FEMA no longer requires survivors to complete an SBA disaster loan application before being considered for any FEMA Other Needs Assistance category, including personal property and transportation - that prerequisite was removed as part of FEMA's 2024 Individual Assistance overhaul. For disasters declared before that date, the older rule still governs accounts still working through recovery: survivors referred to the SBA must complete (not accept) the loan application to remain eligible for Personal Property Assistance, Transportation Assistance, and Group Flood Insurance Policy coverage. Either way, completing an SBA application never obligates the applicant to accept the loan if approved, and it can open the door to further assistance FEMA itself can't cover.

dead_ends.action: Tell a disaster survivor who doesn't want a loan to ignore or discard an SBA disaster loan application referral, assuming it can't affect their FEMA money
dead_ends.why_fails: For any disaster declared before March 22, 2024, FEMA's own guidance states that a survivor referred to the SBA must complete an SBA disaster loan application to be eligible for Personal Property Assistance, Transportation Assistance and/or Group Flood Insurance Policy (GFIP) - ignoring the referral forfeits those specific categories, even though the survivor never has to accept the loan itself.
dead_ends.condition: Disaster declared before March 22, 2024, survivor referred to SBA
dead_ends.common_misconception: That because FEMA money 'doesn't have to be repaid,' anything mentioning the SBA is optional busywork that can be safely thrown away.

dead_ends.action: Tell a survivor of a disaster declared in 2024 or later that they must still apply for or accept an SBA loan before FEMA will help them
dead_ends.why_fails: FEMA's Individual Assistance overhaul, effective for disasters declared on or after March 22, 2024, removed the SBA-application prerequisite entirely: FEMA states it 'doesn't require survivors to apply for an SBA loan before being considered for FEMA assistance,' and applicants can apply to FEMA, SBA, or both at the same time.
dead_ends.common_misconception: That the older, pre-2024 SBA-referral requirement carried over unchanged into current disaster declarations.

workarounds.action: Check the disaster's declaration date before assuming which rule applies, and when in doubt, complete the SBA application anyway - completing it is never a promise to accept the loan
workarounds.how: Apply for FEMA assistance at DisasterAssistance.gov and, if referred, complete the SBA application at SBA.gov/disaster; if SBA later determines the applicant doesn't qualify for a loan, that denial can itself trigger a referral back to FEMA for other assistance.
workarounds.condition: Survivor referred to SBA regardless of declaration date

workarounds.action: For disasters declared on/after March 22, 2024, apply to FEMA and SBA in parallel from the start rather than waiting on a referral, since neither is a prerequisite for the other anymore
